rhythm.cutGrid: No reliable grid (tempo confidence 0.55, downbeat confidence 0.17). Opening half (to the turn): holds of 0.6-1.6 s on lettering and interface, cut on the text, not the beat. After the near-silence and re-entry: holds of 0.9-4 s; place hard cuts within 80 ms after a beat when nothing else decides them, and one cut about 6 frames before the music re-enters at peak level.

style: Light, cool, centred: near-white grounds, one saturated accent ground, dark navy lettering and an accent colour on the brand word, a blurred accent light as the sole ornament; real interface at reading scale with hard punch-ins; a loading shimmer in a contrasting hue is the one off-palette accent.

keep: Hook by scale: one word pulled back from about 2.5x to reading size on expo.out in 14 frames, then a light that uncovers the name
Premise split into one-line phrases, each smaller than the last, landing at the interface's own lettering size before dissolving into it
Interface shown by hard reframes (about 1.8x, then wide, then a macro of the next button, later a same-scale sideways jump) instead of animated zooms
Accelerating drift out of a shot and the same direction continued into the next
Proof as the answer arriving: status hold, then a placeholder that grows from the reply point into the whole result
Near-silence under the opening proof and a cut within the riser, about 6 frames before the music returns
Benefit rows ticked in turn, 7-9 frames apart
Last frame held with text, no fade
mustChange: Branding: wordmark, name, colours if they are the reference brand's, watermark
Music: use a licensed or original track; recreate solely the stop-and-return structure
Graphics: the interface must be the new offering's own screens, captured for real; do not reuse the reference's screens, placeholder gradient colours or floating squares as-is
Copy: every line, prompt and answer written for the new brand
Typeface choice if it is the reference's identity face
